selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What is the main message the teacher gives about why the palace was made?
questions.answer: The palace was made so the king would be known, appreciated, loved, obeyed, thanked, and recognized as the only true owner of all that is in it.

questions.question: What response is expected from the people when they see the beauty and decoration in the palace?
questions.answer: They should value the king’s craftsmanship and admire what he has made.

questions.question: How should the people respond to the king’s mercy and kindness shown through his gifts?
questions.answer: They should show respect by being grateful.

questions.question: What do the special marks placed on each work show about the king?
questions.answer: They show that everything belongs to him, comes from him, and points to his oneness and independence.

questions.question: After hearing the teacher’s words, how did the people divide?
questions.answer: They split into two groups.

questions.question: What did the first group understand when they looked at the palace?
questions.answer: They understood that it had a serious purpose and was not made for pointless entertainment.

questions.question: How did the first group speak to the teacher?
questions.answer: They greeted him respectfully and asked him to explain what their lord had taught him.

questions.question: What was the result of the first group acting as the king wanted?
questions.answer: The king was pleased with them and welcomed them into another higher palace where they were made permanently happy.

questions.question: What did the second group pay attention to in the palace?
questions.answer: They focused only on eating and bodily pleasure.

questions.question: What actions showed that the second group behaved like animals rather than respectful guests?
questions.answer: They overate, fell into sleep, drank what was not meant for them, became drunk, and caused disturbance.

questions.question: In the teacher’s announcement, what is the first duty of the guests toward the king?
questions.answer: Their first duty is to know and recognize him.

questions.question: How is obedience connected to love in the speech?
questions.answer: Since the king shows love through his favors, the people should answer that love by obeying him.

questions.question: What does the king want to show through the excellence seen in his works?
questions.answer: He wants to show his lofty beauty and perfection.

questions.question: Which idea is stronger than simply saying the king is powerful: that he is one among many, or that he has no equal?
questions.answer: The passage teaches that he has no equal at all.

questions.question: What made the first group able to understand the palace correctly?
questions.answer: Their self-knowledge, intelligence, and upright hearts prepared them to think deeply.

questions.question: What question drove the first group to seek more understanding?
questions.answer: They wanted to know the secret behind the palace and what it really contained in meaning.

questions.question: How did the first group benefit from the teacher’s message?
questions.answer: They listened with care, accepted it sincerely, and shaped their conduct around it.

questions.question: What is the basic character of the second group as they enter the palace?
questions.answer: They are inwardly corrupted and controlled by selfish desire.

questions.question: How did the second group respond to the teacher’s words compared with the first group?
questions.answer: The first group listened and accepted, but the second group shut out the guidance completely.

questions.question: What does the prison sentence show about the seriousness of their behavior?
questions.answer: It shows that their disrespect was not minor but deserving of firm judgment.

questions.question: What does the teacher say the king wants through building and displaying the palace?
questions.answer: He wants the people to know him through what he has shown them.

questions.question: How are the people told to return the king’s favor when they receive his blessings?
questions.answer: They are told to obey him, love him, and thank him.

questions.question: Why does the teacher mention the king’s beauty and perfection?
questions.answer: To show that the people should long to meet him and seek his approval.

questions.question: What should the people conclude from the fact that every work bears a unique sign?
questions.answer: They should conclude that the king is one and has no partner or rival.

title: Parable Invitation by the Explaining Master and Conduct of the Two Groups
